Incredible Brunch Views and a Vibrant Late-Night Vibe!

Élephante is an absolutely fantastic spot for brunch in Santa Monica. The open terrace offers beautiful ocean views and a great breeze that make for a perfect morning setting. I ordered the Eggs Benedict, which was excellent and unique—it comes served on a crispy hash brown patty with avocado. It was incredibly satisfying and super filling!

The atmosphere completely shifts in the evening, and it becomes a major hotspot. I went back around 11:30 PM on a weekend hoping to grab a late-night order of their Cacio e Pepe, and the place was totally packed with great energy. A huge bonus for this spot is that their kitchen actually stays open until 1:30 AM! I originally planned to wait for the crowd to thin out a bit, but I ended up getting too tired and calling it a night before ordering.
I’ll definitely be back for that Cacio e Pepe next time.

I highly recommend checking this place out, whether you want a relaxed, scenic brunch or a lively night out!

Excellent experience. We started with the roasted beet and yogurt dip with flatbread; it's a nice appetizer portion and it was the perfect starter. We continued with the tomato and peach salad; it was really well balanced. Then came the oxtail "dumplings" (which are actually tortellini); they had a really nice and deep flavor. Our main course was the lamb shank with sweet potato puree, with a side of cheesey potatoes; the lamb was tender enough to fall of the bone, while the potatoes were nice and creamy. We finished the night with a strawberry ricotta crostata with a little ice cream; once again, everything worked really well together. We also enjoyed some quite tart but pleasent nebbiolo red wine.

The service was really attentive and quick. Our waitress explained everything very thoroughly and all the dishes came out promptly and orderly. I do wish they disclosed upfront the price of the off-menu items they try to sell (i.e.: the desserts).

The atmosphere is somewhat elegant but still casual. Our table however was very close to the open kitchen and we could hear the waiters calling out orders throughout the whole night.

We spent $177.66 after tax before tip for two and it was absolutely worth it.

Tar & Roses was an absolutely fantastic experience. You can taste the passion and attention to detail in every bite.

It's not all that often that a meal significantly exceeds my expectations. I appreciate food that's well-executed, but usually just acknowledge "yes, this was made correctly," right? But every course at Tar & Roses surprised me. Not only was everything executed immaculately, it was all absolutely inspired.

The best bite on the table was the Thai green curry style corn. It sounds simple, but you wanna talk about a balanced dish? Every flavor came through with such clarity, it was absolutely stunning.

We also got the oxtail dumplings, lamb shank, roast duck, broccolini, sticky toffee pudding, and a strawberry tart. Everything was absolutely delicious. Most dishes have a subtle but brilliant fusion twist. Nothing crazy, more of like a - why aren't more people doing this?!

Our server was so friendly, the restaurant was very cozy with great lighting. I mean, no notes, absolutely. It was a first-class dinner. I can't wait to come back.

We had an absolutely fantastic date night at Water Grill in Santa Monica! The entire experience felt upscale, lively, and incredibly memorable.

We started the evening with some of their cocktails, which were exceptionally tasty, unique, and beautifully crafted. For appetizers, we shared a sushi roll and the grilled octopus. The octopus was the absolute star of the start of our meal—perfectly charred and completely fantastic!

For entrees, the cioppino was amazing. It was rich, incredibly flavorful, and packed to the brim with all sorts of delicious, fresh seafood. I originally had my heart set on the Chilean sea bass, but since they were completely out of it for the night, I opted for the lobster roll instead. It turned out to be a blessing in disguise because it was absolutely delicious and packed with tender meat.

The atmosphere has beautiful views of the water and a great, energetic vibe. While the ambiance was a bit on the louder side, it didn't detract at all from the beautiful setting and great energy. To top it all off, the service was good and highly knowledgeable; our server gave us great insights into the menu.

We will definitely be back for another date night soon!

Traveling for work allows me the opportunity to try lots of restaurants.  Some of my co-workers and I ventured to Water Grill for dinner after a long day of being in a conference room.  We made the short walk to Water Grill for some seafood.

We started with chilled wild jumbo Mexican shrimp.  I also ordered a ½ pound of chilled mussels.  We also split a salad.  For my main I ordered the wild Ross Sea Chilean sea bass with butternut squash gnocchi and sage brown butter.  Two of my friends got the tagarashi seared bigeye tuna.  They said it was rather spicy probably since tagarashi means “seven flavor chili pepper.”  My other friend also ordered the sea bass but she got the gluten-free version which came with grilled vegetables.  We were too full to get dessert.  I know...shocking because I love dessert.  But fret not....I came back for Round 2 the next day.

Yes, I came back the next day for lunch after a serious power walk on the beach.   This time I came in for a late lunch and sat up at the bar.  I ordered the chilled mussels again, a bowl of the claim chowder and the jumbo lump crab cake.  I was hungry!  I also ordered the key lime pie to go.  The New England-style chowder was topped with a few little neck clams.  The crab cake had a little spicy kick to it but it wasn’t overpowering. It was a lot of crab meat and not a lot of filler, just the way I like it.  I had the key lime pie later and it had the right amount of tartness one expects in a key lime pie with a huge amount of meringue topping.

If you’re in the mood for seafood, I recommend Water Grill.  It also has a patio so you can enjoy the California coast line and the Pacifica Ocean.

My birthday experience at Loulou Rooftop Restaurant & Lounge (brunch) honestly wasn’t one of the best.

Even worse, the cocktails were terrible. We tried an Old Fashioned that tasted mostly like water, and the Palomas were way too sour. After that, we decided not to order more drinks because we didn’t want to keep getting disappointed.

As for the service, it wasn’t bad, but it definitely wasn’t outstanding either. We basically saw our waitress about three times.

Honestly, the price does not justify the experience. I would recommend it for the vibe and pictures, but if you’re looking for great food, drinks, and an overall memorable dining experience, I wouldn’t recommend it.

Had the pleasure of dining at LouLou Rooftop Restaurant & Lounge in Santa Monica and really enjoyed the experience. The space is absolutely beautiful with a fun Tulum-inspired vibe. I can only imagine how stunning it becomes later in the evening when the sun goes down and all the lights come on, it seems like the kind of place that completely transforms at night.

What stood out most was the teamwork among the staff. Everyone was helping each other, which created such a welcoming atmosphere. Our server, Sophie, was an absolute sweetheart. She took her time explaining menu items, answered all of our questions, and delivered genuinely professional service throughout the meal.

As someone who loves trying a little bit of everything, we ordered quite a few dishes. I always joke that a bigger table is better because I tend to order enough food for four people, even when dining for two! The team quickly accommodated us by bringing another table over, which was appreciated. The Caesar salad was flavorful, generously dressed, and far from dry. The Hamachi Crudo was incredibly fresh and one of my favorite dishes of the evening. The escargot was delicious as well, though slightly overcooked for my taste. We also tried two pizzas, the dough was excellent with a great texture and flavor, although I would have loved to see a few more topping options. Even with there toppings it was not well placed all the mushrooms were on 1 slice and the meat was scattered (not evenly made).

Overall, a very enjoyable dining experience with great food, beautiful surroundings, and wonderful hospitality. Looking forward to coming back and experiencing the rooftop after dark.

The honesty with which the owner represents his restaurant is both refreshing and rewarding. I had the opportunity to try Orto, by chance, because I was staying at the Marriott Courtyard on 5th and Colorado and I wanted a good Italian meal. Orto was a couple of blocks away, so convenience created my choice. Well, as I said, I wanted a good Italian meal, but as luck would have it, I stumbled upon a great Italian meal. The ambiance is inviting. Stone walls, easy lighting, and exceptional "old school" music (i.e. Dean Martin for one). It is an intimate and comfortable seating arrangement.
Andrea, the owner, is there to welcome you with a sincere combination of personable and professional demeanor.
And of course, of utmost importance, the food. Let me say this: I went there on Wednesday evening for dinner and I went back the next night for dinner again. Yes, it was that pleasurable, it was that good. The olive oil was young and fresh, the bread warm and crusty, a Caesar salad done with crouton dust (no crouton chunks here), and pastas prepared exactly as you would enjoy at a cafe in Tuscany.
Is it a bit pricy, yes. Is it worth it, absolutely. It's a discovery waiting for you to happen upon and I can't wait to happen upon it again.

The pricing was very misleading. The ribeye was an extra $10 and the Wagyu ribeye was an extra $25, but the additional charges were written in very small text underneath the dishes, basically the same size as the sauce and other option descriptions. The way it was presented made it look more like an optional add on or side charge rather than an extra charge for choosing that steak. The food was also disappointing. There was grit and sand in the salad, and the shrimp had a really strong fishy smell and did not taste fresh. The steak was extremely undercooked. The center was basically raw and the meat was very difficult to chew.

The chocolate cake also had a noticeable refrigerator taste, like it had been sitting in the fridge for a while.

Our final bill for four people ended up being over $500. For that price, the quality of the food and the overall experience were nowhere near what we expected. Completely not worth the money and we definitely would not come back.

I had one of the most frustrating dining experiences I can remember at this restaurant. From the moment we sat down, the service was painfully slow—so slow that it didn’t feel accidental. Tables that surrounded us were served first, while we waited an unreasonable amount of time just to get water, let alone place an order. It genuinely felt like we were being ignored on purpose.

What made the experience even worse was the clear sense of ageism. The server was noticeably more attentive, friendly, and responsive to younger customers, while treating us with a sarcastic smile that made it feel intentional. To add to the frustration, the appetizer arrived before the drinks—which, in fact, never arrived at all. After waiting long enough, we gave up and asked for the bill, only to find that the drinks had been charged anyway. I had to point it out and say, “The drinks never came, and that’s why we are leaving.” He didn’t respond at all—not even a simple apology.

The food was decent, but not nearly worth the overall experience.

I would not recommend this place to anyone expecting fair treatment or even basic, respectful service.

We had a wonderful lunch at North Italia in Santa Monica and left full and very happy.

I ordered the Crushed Meatball Ragu, which was flavorful, rich and absolutely delicious. I also had the meatballs as an appetizer, and they were excellent. Our son has celiac disease, so eating safely is extremely important to us. The restaurant was able to prepare gluten-free penne with Bolognese sauce for him, and he really enjoyed it.

My wife ordered the Little Gem Caesar with chicken, which was also very good. The chicken was initially missing, and my appetizer arrived a little later than expected, but both issues were handled quickly and professionally. Small mistakes can happen, and the attentive way the staff resolved them gave us no reason to take away a star.

We especially appreciated that the team appeared knowledgeable about gluten-free requirements and took our son’s needs seriously. Based on our experience, North Italia is a very good option for guests with celiac disease. Of course, anyone with celiac disease should always speak directly with the staff and confirm the current preparation procedures, as menus and kitchen practices can change.

The restaurant has a stylish and welcoming atmosphere, the service is attentive and professional, and the location is fantastic—just a short walk from the beach. We left the restaurant completely satisfied and happily headed back toward the ocean.

Delicious food, a great atmosphere and very considerate service. A well-deserved five stars!

The apps were good, flavored well and came with several dipping options! My negative is with the pizza. It may just be that I wasn’t expecting it, but the crust was a bit thicker than typical margherita pizzas from Italian restaurants. It also lacked basil.

My family got two of the pastas, they enjoyed them but expressed it could use some additional salt and seasonings.

I wouldn’t consider the pricing outrageous, but it is by no means affordable and I think based on that, the portion sizes (pastas were a bit small), and the taste of the food, I’m ultimately giving it a 3/5.

text.text:
Ivy at the Shore is one of those classic spots that has stood the test of time. The ambiance is charming, the patio is beautiful, and the service was warm and attentive from start to finish. It's the kind of place that feels quintessentially Santa Monica and is always great for out-of-town guests, a casual date, or a leisurely lunch by the beach.

The drinks were definitely a highlight and one of my favorite parts of the meal. Well-balanced, refreshing, and a great complement to the seafood-focused menu.

For food, we shared the crab cakes, soft shell crab, and tuna tartare. The crab cakes were delicious, packed with crab and nicely cooked, while the soft shell crab was crispy and satisfying. I also appreciated that the tuna tartare was served with cucumber slices instead of the usual chips or crackers—it felt lighter, fresher, and let the tuna shine.

My main hesitation is the value. While the food was good, the portions felt a bit small for the price, and I left wishing there was a little more substance for what we paid. Everything was enjoyable, but not quite memorable enough to justify the premium pricing.

Overall, Ivy at the Shore remains a classic Los Angeles institution with great service, beautiful ambiance, and excellent cocktails. I'd happily come back for the atmosphere and drinks alone, but I'm giving it 4 stars for now based on the overall value.
